source.title: Fact vs fiction--how paratextual information shapes our reading processes

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed neuroimaging study, verified via PubMed (PMID 22956671). This is the OTHER half of the inconsistency MECH-542's notes record, and banking both is the point. Here a factual label produced 'an activation pattern suggesting an action-based reconstruction' with faster responses, while a fictional label produced 'a constructive simulation of what might have happened' -- i.e. a distinct processing signature by source framing, the finding Hartung et al. 2017 (n=1,742) then failed to reproduce behaviourally. Direction 'mixed' because the pair does not resolve: a small imaging study finds a difference, a large behavioural study finds none, and they measure different things. Confidence 0.48 -- the effect is real as reported but its status is exactly the unsettled one the claim already describes, and it must not be cited as establishing that source framing switches processing mode.
failure_signatures: If the fact/fiction processing difference is real but appears only in neural measures and not in behaviour, then MECH-542's update-fingerprint assay must measure internal update directly; a behavioural-only REE assay would reproduce Hartung's null and wrongly conclude the claim is false.

The two studies differ in measure, sample size and manipulation, so neither refutes the other. A REE write-up citing Altmann alone would overstate the evidence for source-sensitive processing; citing Hartung alone would overstate its absence. Both belong in any statement of the claim's external status.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Narratives identical in content but labelled factual versus fictional were read differently: the factual mode engaged an activation pattern the authors interpret as action-based reconstruction, with faster behavioural responses, whereas the fictional mode engaged a pattern interpreted as constructive simulation of what might have happened, paralleling the imagination of hypothetical scenarios.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the positive half of MECH-542's external picture: a source label, holding content constant, changes how the material is processed. It is consistent with source-sensitive permeability but does not by itself distinguish selective permeability from mode-switching, and it is not consistently reproduced.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Small-sample neuroimaging with reverse-inference interpretation of activation patterns; German-language literary stimuli; the dependent variable is processing style during reading, not which downstream variables were permitted to update -- which is MECH-542's actual content. The finding was not reproduced behaviourally at scale (Hartung et al. 2017, banked alongside).
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI; readers of short narratives labelled factual or fictional by paratextual framing.

confidence_components.notes: Good journal, but small-n imaging with interpretive activation mapping, and superseded in scale by a null. Deliberately scored low so it cannot carry the claim on its own.
